headline: XRP Ledger patches decade-old unlimited-minting bug as markets drift on flash-crash anniversary
summary: A critical vulnerability in the XRP Ledger — one that could have allowed an attacker to mint billions of dollars worth of XRP from nothing — was quietly patched, making it the day's most consequential story even as XRP itself barely moved. Meanwhile, markets marked one year since the 2025 flash crash that wiped $19 billion in minutes: Bitcoin and Ethereum liquidity have largely recovered, but altcoins remain structurally thin. NEAR Protocol bucked the drift with a nearly 9% gain, while most of the top 15 ended the session within 1% of yesterday's close.

winners.name: NEAR Protocol
winners.catalyst: NEAR surged roughly 9% on the one-year anniversary of the 2025 flash crash, likely driven by altcoin rotation as the Fear & Greed index climbed to 64 and traders reassessed undervalued layer-1 assets. No single news catalyst was identified.

losers.name: Canton
losers.catalyst: Canton fell nearly 5% with no specific news catalyst; the decline likely reflects thin liquidity and the broader structural fragility in altcoin markets flagged by analysts on the flash-crash anniversary.

whyItMoved:
Today's session was defined more by what didn't happen than what did. Bitcoin slipped 0.57% to $82,803 and Ethereum edged down 0.44% to $2,495 — both moves well within noise. The Fear & Greed index sits at 64 (Greed), suggesting the broader mood remains constructive even if price action is quiet.

The anniversary of the October 10, 2025 flash crash — which erased $19 billion in market value in minutes — gave analysts a natural checkpoint. The verdict: Bitcoin and Ethereum market depth has rebuilt to healthy levels, but altcoin liquidity remains thin. That structural fragility likely explains why Canton dropped nearly 5% on no news at all; in shallow markets, small sell orders move prices sharply.

NEAR Protocol was the clear outlier, gaining 8.94% without a specific catalyst. The most plausible explanation is altcoin rotation: as sentiment improved and traders looked beyond large-cap assets, layer-1 networks that had underperformed attracted fresh capital. NEAR had lagged its peers in recent weeks, making it a natural target for that rotation.

Solana fell 1.29% and Monero dropped 2.67%, both without obvious news drivers — consistent with the thin-liquidity picture analysts flagged today. Hyperliquid also slid 2.35%, continuing a soft stretch for the decentralized exchange token.
worthKnowing: The XRP Ledger patched a decade-old vulnerability that could have allowed an attacker to mint an unlimited supply of XRP — effectively printing billions of dollars worth of the asset from nothing — before it was ever exploited.

New York's Attorney General secured up to $35 million and a lifetime crypto industry ban from Celsius founder Alex Mashinsky, drawing a formal close to one of the largest enforcement cases from the 2022 lending-platform collapse.

Ledger is investigating a wave of wallet drains tied to buyers of a product called CryptoBilis, with estimated losses exceeding $86 million — a reminder that hardware wallet security depends on the full supply chain, not just the device itself.
Robinhood Chain saw transaction volumes fall more than 40%, a sharp contraction for the retail-focused layer-2 network that signals weakening user engagement since its launch.
